extracted.intended_audience: United States Indian agents, Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and federal policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and metrics used in 1880 annual reports for assessing the condition and administration of Indian agencies (agriculture, schools, health, policing, infrastructure, economy, and tribal governance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural crop condition and yields
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates and assessments of crop performance (wheat, oats, corn, potatoes, turnips, pumpkins, squashes, garden vegetables), including bushels per acre and overall condition (e.g., "I estimate them at ten bushels per acre. Wheat (uncut) I estimate at 15 bushels").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes causes of failure or lateness (frequent rains, late planting, immature corn/potatoes), gives per-acre yield estimates, and uses thrashing results as basis for estimates. Includes comparisons with prior years and qualitative judgments ("average crop", "comparative failure").

rubrics_metrics.name: Acres broken and acreage under cultivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of acres broken, newly broken, and cultivated by agency and individual families (e.g., acres broken this season, agency farm acres, individual family tracts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks both agency and promiscuous Indian plots, reports planned acreage for next year, and recommends contracting for breaking additional acreage (recommendation to let contract for breaking 300 acres).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency farm output and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Production and handling on the agency farm (bushels thrashed, hay secured, corn/potato estimates, herd sufficient for beef), and staffing (agency farmer and assistant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports exact amounts thrashed (e.g., "2,261 bushels of wheat, 249 bushels of oats, and 66 bushels of rye"), remaining unthrashed crop, and emphasizes daily employment of Indians for sowing and reaping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian participation in farming and labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which Indian families work their patches and the agency (number of families working, willingness to work, number of daily labor applicants, apprenticeships).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes cultural/practical impediments (hunting expeditions, migration), praises good conduct where present, and quantifies potential (e.g., "readily till next year 300 acres if it was broken and ready to plant").

rubrics_metrics.name: School establishment, attendance, and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of day and boarding schools, months in operation, average attendance, and obstacles to success (e.g., families leaving for hunting, building destroyed by fire).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports capacities and attendance (boarding-school capacity 60 but average attendance 15; industrial boarding-school capacity 102 with 82 attendance part-year), links attendance to stability of families, and describes distribution of rations when boarding school unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial education and apprenticeships
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and success of industrial training (shops: mill, blacksmith, carpenter, harness-shop; apprenticeships; brick-yard), employment of Indians as apprentices and skilled workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records numbers employed/apprenticed, types of trades taught, mission and government school roles, and notes that apprentices are usually in demand ("always have more applicants than I can accommodate").

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing quality and household improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Number and condition of dwellings (frame houses, additions, wells, cellars, carpeting), family contributions to building, and desire to improve housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents specific improvements (e.g., "Two new frame houses...", individual cash contributions $15–$50), and treats housing improvement as evidence of progress toward civilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency infrastructure and buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence and condition of agency buildings and facilities (school-house cost, commissary, granaries, shops, mill, jail, stables, grist-mill), and need for additional employee housing or repairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists structures, reports damages (e.g., industrial school building destroyed by fire), and calls for construction (physician's quarters, additional employee buildings) when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Livestock counts and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers of ponies, horses, agency cattle, and purchases or distributions of stock; production of hay for feed and sales of hay to settlers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports counts (e.g., "about 400 ponies and horses... and 300 head of agency cattle"), purchases (thirty-six farm horses bought and distributed), and ties stock management to self-sufficiency and excuses for labor/non-labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fencing, trespass, and crop destruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent and quality of fencing (barbed wire miles/rods), incidents of white stock grazing on reserves, and resulting crop destruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records fencing built ("fenced nearly 400 acres with barbed wire... about 1,300 rods") and cites failures of inadequate fences leading to destroyed fields; implies fence quality is a metric of agency protection and farm success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horse theft and external depredations
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidence of horse theft from Indians, suspected involvement of professional thieves and local accomplices, and the impact on tribal stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative evidence used to infer organized theft ("best horses are stolen"), and notes that once stock is lost it is rarely recovered; indicates need for policing and legal remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Police efficiency and law enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization, discipline, and effectiveness of Indian police (arrests made, insufficient organization, fatal incidents during arrests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates police by outcomes and discipline, cites specific incidents (killing of an Indian by chief of police), and recommends improvements in police system organization and discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary condition, health metrics, and medical provisioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Health status of the tribe: epidemics (measles, typho-malarial, scarlet fever), mortality rates, births/deaths counts, causes (malaria from pooled water, infant practices), and availability/timeliness of medical supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for physician quarters with clinical room and dispensary, records that direct medical supervision reduces mortality, and links sanitation, water quality, and infant care practices to mortality statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortality and vital statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of births and deaths during the year, with emphasis on infant mortality as an indicator of sanitary conditions (e.g., "There have occurred 25 births and 33 deaths").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses mortality comparative statements ("mortality less than last year"), attributes causes, and uses these figures to justify medical infrastructure and public-health measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-support and economic dependency
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which tribes are self-supporting versus reliant on government funds or annuities, and how tribal funds (large annuities) affect labor incentives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that large cash annuities can discourage manual labor and retard advancement ("the large cash annuity... is the greatest obstacle to its advancement"), and suggests rethinking disposition of abundant funds without violating government good faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land-title security and legal protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence or lack of permanent legal title for Indian occupants and its effect on willingness to invest in homes and agriculture (Santee request for lasting title).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames insecure land titles as a principal hindrance to self-support and settlement, and recommends legislation to vest titles in Indians to promote stability and improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community governance and political organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure of tribal governance (election of councillors vs. chiefs for life), presence of schisms, councils, and the effect of leadership changes on cooperation and labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links tribal unity and administrative conduct (schisms, jealousies, removals) to agricultural productivity and retention of members; highlights successful use of inspectors/agents to restore discipline and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission activity and religious/educational influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Role and capacity of missionary schools and churches (American Board of Foreign Missions, Episcopal schools, Friends' industrial school) in education and industrial training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports capacities, attendance numbers, the types of instruction (industrial arts, agricultural instruction for boys, domestic for girls), and notes missions' constructive role in teacher/ministers production and local employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance, capacity and condition of boarding/industrial schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical capacity of industrial/boarding schools, average attendance, condition of buildings (e.g., burned industrial school), and local distribution of rations when boarding not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses attendance relative to capacity as a measure of success (e.g., capacity 102 with 82 attendance), notes building repairs/ reconstruction needed, and links boarding attendance to children's educational progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural timing and seed quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of timely planting and good seed for crop success (late sowing and poor seed caused short crops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compares seasons and practices across years and states that improved timing and seed led to better crops, recommending attention to planting times and seed quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic accounting and expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting of expenditures and tribal/government financial support (e.g., amounts spent for beef, appropriations for schooling, funds used for fences, purchase of horses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses explicit figures ("only $33.86 having been expended during the past year for beef", $200 annual appropriations) to judge fiscal management and reliance on tribal funds versus government aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure maintenance and transport impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects of railroads and infrastructure on agency security and settlement (railroad provides convenience and an avenue for thieves), and maintenance burdens (e.g., keeping a dam against wash).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighs benefits (transport, market access) against increased exposure to vagrants/thieves; documents maintenance difficulties for key works (dam washing away) as operational challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators of moral and social condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative measures of morality and social order (presence/absence of illegitimacy, profanity, drunkenness, murders, general disposition toward whites).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses such indicators to argue for or against 'civilization' progress ("The moral condition of the Otoes is in many respects above the average Indian"), and ties social behavior to success of schooling and labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for administrative action
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit policy or operational recommendations directed at the Commissioner or superiors (e.g., abstain/engage with Sitting Bull, let contract for breaking land, build physician quarters, vest land titles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete suggested actions with justifications drawn from observed conditions (e.g., rejecting Sitting Bull's terms due to orders, but stating a treaty could have been made; recommending letting a contract to break 300 acres; urging legislation to vest titles).
